column3: Failure in which the thin metal panel tears over the screw head as the girt rotates.

column3: Reinforcement of the metal panel at the fastener by rigid board insulation, which suppresses local panel deformation and prevents panel pull-over.

column3: Polyisocyanurate rigid board insulation with a compressive yield plateau near 23 psi; the only rigid board used in the vacuum box tests.

Midspan moment at failure, computed as D(L_g x 12)^2/8 from the uniform line load D derived from the peak chamber pressure plus panel and girt self weight.

column6: Tested upside down so that girt deformation could be observed.

Cold-formed steel roof secondary member spanning between frames and supporting the steel deck; here always one of two parallel lines 5 ft apart.

column3: A recorded step of the test, identified by a load number, at which the vacuum was held at least 5 minutes and all instrumentation scanned.

column3: Local instability of a purlin in an end span, the observed limit state of both uplift systems; its direction of rotation (clockwise/counterclockwise looking south) was recorded.

column6: Reported as an incidental, unwanted failure mode in the vacuum box tests and attributed to stripped threads or re-used purlin holes.

A simulated test with more than one panel, two supports and a screwed-down perimeter, loaded by negative pressure inside a wooden vacuum chamber.

column6: Coined in this work; identified at about grade 70 for ASTM 607-85.

column3: The standardized normal (Z) value of each test load used to identify data points beyond 1.96 standard deviations for rejection; 'composita' is the paper's term for the sorted Z series.

column3: Ratio of the measured test moment to the computed nominal section moment; the dimensionless output of the base test.

The in-plane shear strength and stiffness of the roof sheeting, measured by the AISI cantilever diaphragm test; AISI requires at least 2000 lb/in. stiffness or lateral deflection under span/360.
Edge member (a 1/4" x 3" x 3" continuous angle in the standard procedure, 1.5 x 1.5 x 0.12 in. in these tests) placed at the panel ends to represent the building eave strut.

Total nominal diaphragm shear strength including the eave member, S_nt = S_n + S_e, with the eave contribution isolated and added rather than scaled with diaphragm size.
Relative movement at the panel side laps, identified as the dominant source of diaphragm stiffness loss in standing seam roofs.

column3: The single span, two purlin line roof system test, built of the same components as the actual multispan roof, loaded uniformly in uplift to failure.

Moment that causes tension in the top flange of the purlin under uplift loading; maximum value generally occurs near the midspan of an end bay.

Predicted failure load of the three-span system, taken as the minimum of M_us x 100 plf / M- and M_AISI x 100 plf / M+.
The nominal uniform load applied in the stiffness analysis of the multispan system, used only to scale moments.
Effective section modulus of the cold-formed purlin, computed per AISI (1996), used with F_y to obtain M_AISI.
The test apparatus: a sealed chamber in which the roof assembly is loaded to failure by air pressure difference, here acting upward (uplift).
Predicted divided by experimental failure load for the confirming test; a value below 1.0 means the prediction is conservative.

The spliced overlap of adjacent purlins at interior supports; length depends on purlin depth (0'-11 3/4"/1'-11 3/4" for 8 in. Z, 1'-5 3/4"/2'-11 3/4" for 9.5 in. Z).
A roof system in which panels are joined by seams and attached to purlins by clips rather than direct through-fasteners, giving reduced lateral restraint.
